name: SG90 micro servo
description: Tiny plastic-gear servo. Fine for a gripper or a very small desk arm, too weak for most arm joints.

name: MG996R metal-gear servo
description: The classic hobby arm servo. Cheap and strong for its size, but it wobbles a little and has no position feedback.

name: DS3218 20 kg digital servo
description: About twice the torque of an MG996R with less wobble. A common shoulder servo for desk arms.

name: DS5160 60 kg servo
description: Large, high-torque hobby servo for the shoulder of a bigger arm. Draws a lot of current.

name: Feetech STS3215 bus servo (7.4 V)
description: Serial bus servo with a 12-bit position sensor, used in the SO-101 arm. All joints share one cable and report their position back.

name: Feetech STS3215 bus servo (12 V)
description: The 12 V version of the STS3215, with more torque. Same cable and software as the 7.4 V one.

name: Dynamixel XL430-W250-T
description: Well-documented smart servo with an absolute encoder and current sensing. Precise, with good ROS support.

name: Dynamixel XM430-W350-T
description: Strong, precise smart servo for the shoulder and elbow of a research-grade arm. Expensive.

name: NEMA 17 stepper motor (0.45 N·m)
description: Standard 3D-printer stepper. Precise and cheap. Used directly on the base, or with a belt or gearbox on the other joints.

name: NEMA 17 stepper with 5:1 planetary gearbox
description: NEMA 17 with a 5.18:1 gearbox: about five times the torque. A good elbow or wrist motor for a stepper arm.

name: NEMA 17 stepper with 27:1 planetary gearbox
description: NEMA 17 with a 26.85:1 gearbox. Slow but strong: the gearbox, not the motor, sets the torque limit.

name: NEMA 23 stepper with 10:1 planetary gearbox
description: Big stepper with a 10:1 gearbox for the shoulder of an arm that lifts around a kilogram. Needs a separate DM542-style driver.

name: NEMA 23 stepper with 20:1 planetary gearbox
description: NEMA 23 with a 20:1 gearbox for a shoulder that lifts a kilogram at arm's length. Slow and strong. Needs a DM542-style driver.

name: Mini claw with SG90 servo
description: Small acrylic claw for light, rigid objects like dice, pens and small parts.

name: Metal claw with MG996R servo
description: Aluminium claw that opens to about 5 cm. Holds cans, boxes and tools up to around half a kilo.

name: Printed parallel gripper with bus servo
description: Two jaws that close straight towards each other, printed from your CAD files and driven by one bus servo. Good for boxes and parts with flat sides.

name: Soft silicone finger gripper
description: Flexible fingers that wrap around fruit, eggs and odd shapes without crushing them.

name: Suction cup, mini vacuum pump and valve
description: A 40 mm cup on the arm, with the pump on the base. Picks up flat, smooth, non-porous things: cards, tiles, phones, sealed boxes.

name: Printed tool holder (pen, laser or camera)
description: A printed clamp that holds a pen, a small laser module or a camera at the end of the arm. Design it in the part designer or download one with your reference design.

name: PCA9685 16-channel servo board
description: Drives up to 16 PWM servos from two I2C pins on an Arduino or ESP32.

name: ESP32 dev board
description: Runs the arm and serves a little web page to move it from your phone.

name: 6 V 10 A power supply
description: Servos draw up to about 2.5 A each when they strain. Never power them from the board's 5 V pin.

name: Bus servo driver board (USB)
description: Connects the servo bus to a computer over USB. LeRobot and the Feetech software both talk to it.

name: ROBOTIS U2D2 and power hub
description: USB adapter and power board for Dynamixel servos. Works with ROS 2 and the Dynamixel SDK.

name: 12 V 5 A power supply
description: Power for 12 V bus servos. Use a 7.4 V 5 A supply instead for 7.4 V servos.

name: Teensy 4.1
description: Fast enough to send smooth step pulses to six motors at once. The AR4 arm uses one.

name: TMC2209 stepper driver
description: Quiet driver for one NEMA 17. One per NEMA 17 joint.

name: DM542 stepper driver
description: Driver for one NEMA 23. One per NEMA 23 joint.

name: Limit switch
description: Steppers don't know where they are at power-on. Each joint drives to a switch to find its zero.

name: 24 V 10 A power supply
description: Power for the stepper drivers. Put an emergency stop button on its output.

name: Turntable bearing (lazy susan)
description: Carries the arm's weight and bending load so the base motor only has to turn it.

name: Emergency stop button
description: Big red button that cuts motor power. Wire it into the power supply output, not the controller.
